---
title: "Getting started"
---

Quartorium is a small Node.js server. One installation serves a whole research group: the
person who runs it connects the group's repositories, and everyone else only ever uses links.

## Requirements

| | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) | 22.13 or newer | Runs the server; uses Node's built-in SQLite (no native modules to compile). |
| [Git](https://git-scm.com/) | 2.38 or newer | All version control; `merge-tree --write-tree` is used to merge without a working copy. |
| [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) | 1.4 or newer | Renders figures and tables; its bundled Pandoc converts text. |
| R / Python | as your papers need | Only for running the papers' code. Not needed if you commit Quarto's `_freeze` folder (see below). |

## Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/andjar/quartorium.git
cd quartorium
npm install
npm run build                         # builds the browser app into frontend/dist
QUARTORIUM_ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-a-password' npm start
```

Open <http://localhost:8000> and log in with the admin password.

For development, run `npm run dev` (the backend and the frontend together) and open
<http://localhost:5173>. Run the tests with `npm test`.

## Connect a repository

On the admin page, click **Connect a repository** and enter its Git URL. Any Git host works:

| Host | URL example | Username | Token |
|---|---|---|---|
| Codeberg / Forgejo / Gitea | `https://codeberg.org/you/paper.git` | your account name | Settings → Applications → access token with repository read/write |
| GitLab (incl. university instances) | `https://gitlab.example.org/group/paper.git` | `oauth2` | personal or project access token with `write_repository` |
| GitHub | `https://github.com/you/paper.git` | anything | fine-grained token with *Contents: read & write* |
| Your own server | `ssh://git@server/srv/git/paper.git` or a path | – | uses the server's SSH key |

The token is needed for private repositories and to push. Quartorium pushes branches named
`quartorium/…`, and keeps your main branch up to date with the review round, so you can
keep pulling and pushing main from RStudio. This can be switched off per repository, for
example when main is protected (see [Git and the paper trail](git.qmd#main)).

## Start your first round

1. On the admin page, click **New review round** next to the repository, pick the `.qmd` file
   and enter the lead author's name (usually yourself).
2. Click **Open as lead**. This is your lead link; bookmark it.
3. In the **People** tab, add your co-authors. **Invite by e-mail** opens your own mail
   program with a short message and their personal link (or the server sends it, if mail is
   configured).

That's it. The [user guide](guide.qmd) explains what happens next.

## Configuration

All settings are environment variables.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `QUARTORIUM_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | *(unset: admin pages off)* | Password for connecting repositories and starting rounds. Links keep working without it. |
| `PORT` | `8000` | Port to listen on. |
| `QUARTORIUM_DATA` | `backend/data` | Database, bare clones of the repositories, and the render cache. Back this up. |
| `QUARTORIUM_PUBLIC_URL` | *(from the request)* | Address people use, e.g. `https://review.example.org`; used for links in e-mails. |
| `QUARTORIUM_SMTP_URL` | *(unset: no e-mail)* | Mail server, e.g. `smtp://user:pass@smtp.example.org:587`. Without it, invitations open the lead's mail program instead. |
| `QUARTORIUM_MAIL_FROM` | `Quartorium <quartorium@localhost>` | Sender of e-mails. |
| `QUARTORIUM_QUARTO` | `quarto` | Path to the Quarto binary. |
| `QUARTORIUM_PANDOC` | `quarto pandoc` | Pandoc command, if you want a different one. |
| `QUARTORIUM_COMMIT_IDLE` | `600` | Seconds without typing after which work in progress is committed (leaving the page commits at once). |
| `QUARTORIUM_SYNC` | `60` | Seconds between checks of the main branch for new commits (a lead opening the paper also checks). |
| `QUARTORIUM_PUSH` | `1` | Set to `0` to never push (for trying things out). |
| `QUARTORIUM_RENDER_TIMEOUT` | `900` | Seconds before a render is stopped. |
| `QUARTORIUM_COMMITTER_NAME` / `_EMAIL` | `Quartorium` | Committer of every commit. The *author* is always the person. |
| `QUARTORIUM_SECRET` | *(generated)* | Signs the admin session cookie; generated into the data folder if unset. |

## Running it for a group

- **Put it behind HTTPS.** Run Quartorium on localhost and put a reverse proxy (Caddy,
  nginx, Apache) in front of it with a certificate. Links are keys, so they must not travel
  over plain HTTP.
- **Keep it running** with systemd, a container, or your platform's process manager.
  Stopping the server cleanly (`SIGTERM`) commits all pending work first.
- **Avoid running code on the server** if you like: use Quarto's
  [`freeze`](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html#freeze) in the paper's
  project and commit the `_freeze` folder. Quarto then uses the stored results, and the
  server needs neither R nor Python. Otherwise, install what the papers need, as you would
  on your own machine.
- **Back up** the data folder. Everything that matters long-term is also in Git, but the
  database holds work that was not committed yet and the links.

A minimal systemd unit:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Quartorium
After=network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/quartorium
Environment=QUARTORIUM_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me
Environment=QUARTORIUM_PUBLIC_URL=https://review.example.org
Environment=QUARTORIUM_DATA=/var/lib/quartorium
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start
Restart=on-failure
User=quartorium

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
